QuestionStmt.S: The logically equivalent statement of $$(\sim p \land q) \lor (\sim p \land \sim q) \lor (p \land \sim q)$$ is

Solution.S:
We simplify step by step:

$$(\sim p \land q) \lor (\sim p \land \sim q) \lor (p \land \sim q)$$

Using distributive law on the first two terms: $(\sim p \land q) \lor (\sim p \land \sim q) = \sim p \land (q \lor \sim q) = \sim p \land T = \sim p$.

Thus the expression becomes:

$$\sim p \lor (p \land \sim q)$$

Now apply distributive law:

$$(\sim p \lor p) \land (\sim p \lor \sim q) = T \land (\sim p \lor \sim q) = \sim p \lor \sim q$$

Therefore the given expression is logically equivalent to $(\sim p) \lor (\sim q)$, which corresponds to option B.
